title: Etale algebras over a normal domain have finitely many normal domain factors
statement: Let $A$ be a normal integral domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and let $B$ be a commutative $A$-algebra for which $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. There exist an integer $n\geq0$, commutative $A$-algebras $B_1,\ldots,B_n$ which are normal integral domains, and an isomorphism of $A$-algebras $B\cong\prod_{j=1}^n B_j$. The empty product is the zero ring, so $B=0$ is allowed. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed on $A$ or $B$.

source.place: Tag 030C (lemma-characterize-reduced-ring-normal), implication (1) to (3), applied to an etale algebra over a domain. Auxiliary consequence: flat going-down puts every minimal prime above (0), and the etale generic fibre has finitely many primes. This combined etale consequence is agent-formulated, not the verbatim statement of 030C.

proof.text: If B is the zero ring, take n=0: the unique map from B to the empty product is an A-algebra isomorphism. Henceforth suppose B is nonzero. This case distinction does not impose any extra hypothesis in the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 030C, empty finite product convention; elementary zero-ring case

proof.text: For every prime p of A, the localization-normal-domain lemma makes A_p a normal domain; hence A is a normal ring by definition. Apply etale normality ascent to A -> B to obtain that B is a normal ring. Thus every B_q is a domain and consequently reduced: if x^m=0 in a domain, repeated cancellation gives x=0. The jointly-injective prime-localizations lemma now gives that B is reduced.

source.place: Tags 00GY, 00GV, 033C and 00HN: normal localizations, etale ascent and detection of reducedness

proof.text: The definition of etale gives that Spec B -> Spec A is locally of finite presentation. Apply the affine-opens finite-presentation lemma to the whole affine opens Spec B and Spec A. By the Spec-map global-sections identification the resulting ring map is the given A -> B. Therefore B is finitely presented, in particular it is generated as an A-algebra by finitely many elements b_1,...,b_r (the images of the presentation variables).

source.place: Tag 01TQ (1) => (2), applied to the whole affine spectra; Schemes Tags 01HV and 01I2 for the natural global-sections identification

proof.text: Put S=A\{0}, K=Frac(A)=S^{-1}A, let W be the image of S in B, and put C=W^{-1}B. The fraction construction gives a K-algebra structure on C by (a/s)(b/t)=ab/(st), where images in B are understood; the fraction equivalence relation makes this well-defined. The images of b_1,...,b_r generate C over K: write any b/t as P(b_1,...,b_r)/t and replace each coefficient a of P by a/t in K. Thus C is a finite-type K-algebra. This constructs the algebra and its generators directly, without invoking a generic-fibre comparison theorem.

source.place: Section Tag 00CM and Definition Tag 07JZ: fraction construction and its operations

proof.text: Every ideal of the field K is either zero or K (a nonzero element of an ideal has an inverse), so K is Noetherian. Since C is a finite-type K-algebra, the finite-type-algebra Noetherian lemma makes C Noetherian. The Noetherian minimal-prime lemma therefore says that C has finitely many minimal primes. No Noetherian assertion about A or B is used.

source.place: Tags 00FN and 00FR: finite-type algebras over Noetherian rings and finite minimal primes

proof.text: Let q be any minimal prime of B, and let p be its contraction to A. The etale-algebra flatness lemma and flat going-down, applied to the primes (0) subset p of the domain A, give a prime q_0 subset q contracting to (0). Minimality of q forces q_0=q, so p=(0). In particular q avoids W: the image of a nonzero s in A cannot belong to q.

source.place: Tag 00HS, flat going-down; etale flatness as in Tag 00U2

proof.text: Apply clause (1) of the general localization-prime correspondence to B -> C and W. For a minimal prime q of B, Step 6 shows q avoids W, so qC is a prime of C with contraction q. It is minimal: if r is a prime of C contained in qC, its contraction is a prime of B contained in q, hence equals q; the inverse identities of the correspondence then give r=qC. Distinct q give distinct qC because contraction recovers q. We have injected the minimal primes of B into the finite set of minimal primes of C from Step 5. Hence B has finitely many minimal primes.

source.place: Tag 00E3: extension and contraction of primes for an arbitrary multiplicative subset; elementary restriction of that bijection to minimal primes

proof.text: The ring B is reduced and normal by Step 2, and has finitely many minimal primes by Step 7. Apply implication (1) => (3) of the reduced-normal total-fractions criterion to B. It gives a finite list of normal integral domains B_1,...,B_n and a ring isomorphism theta:B -> product_j B_j. The reducedness and finite-minimal-prime hypotheses of that criterion have both been verified.

Give each B_j the A-algebra structure a |-> pr_j(theta(a*1_B)). Then theta sends the structure image of a to the tuple of these coordinate images, so theta is an A-algebra homomorphism. Its inverse also respects A because theta is injective and theta(structure_B(a))=structure_product(a). Thus the ring isomorphism in Step 8 is an A-algebra isomorphism. The domains and their normality are unchanged. Together with Step 1 this proves every clause, including n=0 and the absence of any Noetherian hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 030C, elementary transport of the given A-algebra structure along the resulting ring isomorphism

proof_origin.place: Combination of Tags 033C, 00FN, 00FR, 00HS and 00E3 to verify the hypotheses of Tag 030C (1) => (3); the fraction-generation and A-algebra upgrade arguments are written out here.
